questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly to describe an action that has no specific time mentioned?
options: I have lived here since 2010.
I have lived here for five years.
I lived here for five years.
I have lived here since five years.
questions.answer: I have lived here for five years.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form of the adjective 'busy'.
options: busier
more busy
busiest
busierest

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct conditional structure: 'If I ______ enough money, I would buy a new car.'
options: have
had
has
having

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a modal verb to give advice?
options: You should to rest more.
You should rest more.
You must rest more.
You ought to rest more.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses a gerund after the preposition 'enjoy'.
options: I enjoy swimming in the lake.
I enjoy to swim in the lake.
I enjoy swim in the lake.
I enjoy swimming at the lake.
questions.answer: I enjoy swimming in the lake.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct past continuous tense?
options: They were playing football when it started to rain.
They play football when it started to rain.
They played football when it started to rain.
They were playing football while it started to rain.
questions.answer: They were playing football when it started to rain.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that uses the correct infinitive after 'want'.
options: She wants to go to the cinema.
She wants going to the cinema.
She wants go to the cinema.
She wants to going to the cinema.
questions.answer: She wants to go to the cinema.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct linker to show contrast?
options: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
It was raining, but we stayed outside.
It was raining, therefore we stayed inside.
It was raining, however we stayed outside.
questions.answer: It was raining, but we stayed outside.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct superlative form: 'This is the ______ book I have ever read.'
options: interesting
more interesting
most interesting
interestingest

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect to indicate an action completed before another past action?
options: I had finished my homework before dinner.
I finished my homework before I had dinner.
I have finished my homework before dinner.
I had finished my homework before I ate dinner.
questions.answer: I had finished my homework before dinner.
